Your first month, step by step

Nothing to prepare. Here is how most new students settle in.

  1. Week 1

    Arrive and breathe

    Learn the basics of breathing and simple standing poses in a beginner class.

  2. Week 2

    Build your base

    Add strength and balance. Your teacher shows easier or harder options for each pose.

  3. Week 3

    Find your flow

    Link poses with your breath and try a second style, such as Vinyasa or Yin.

  4. Week 4

    Make it a habit

    Pick a routine that fits your week, in the studio or online, and keep it going.

Yoga that fits real life

You do not need to be flexible or experienced. Our teachers keep classes small, explain every move clearly and offer an easier or harder option for each one.

BreathEvery class starts with breathing to settle the mind.
MovementSafe, steady poses that build strength and ease.
RestWe always end with time to be still.

Before your first class

Find a quick answer, or ask us directly.

Still have a question?

We usually reply within an hour during opening times.

Message on WhatsApp
I am a complete beginner. Is that okay?

Yes. Beginner classes are our most popular, and every teacher shows easier options for each pose.

What should I bring?

Comfortable clothes you can stretch in and a water bottle. Mats, blocks and blankets are provided.

How early should I arrive?

Come 10 minutes early for your first class so you can meet your teacher, find a spot and settle in.

Is my first class really free?

Yes. Your first class is free, with no card needed. Book it using the form below.

I have an injury or am pregnant. Can I join?

Usually yes. Tell your teacher before class so they can adjust poses for you, and check with your doctor if you are unsure.

Can I join online?

Most classes stream live and are recorded, so you can practice from home at any time.

What is the cancellation policy?

Cancel any booking up to 4 hours before class at no cost. Memberships can be paused at any time.
